what.heading: What Apercura does
body: Apercura publishes a page for every doctor, dentist and midwife registered in France, built from the national register of health professionals and other public open data.

Patients find any practitioner, not only those who pay a platform. Practitioners can claim their page for free, check it and complete it. Free online booking, without a patient account, will open later.

principles.heading: Principles
list: Every practitioner is listed the same way, whether or not they use Apercura.
Factual information only: no ratings, no reviews, no ads and no paid ranking.
Free for practitioners and patients, with no subscription and no commission.
Each page shows where its facts come from and when they were last updated.
Minimal data, collected for a stated purpose and deleted on schedule.

how.heading: Where the pages come from
body: Pages are generated each week from the Annuaire Santé of the Agence du numérique en santé, the FINESS register of establishments and the Assurance Maladie directory. The data page lists every source, its licence and its date.

who.heading: Who runs Apercura
body: Apercura is a public-interest project. It is not a government service and is not affiliated with the Assurance Maladie, the Ordres or the Agence du numérique en santé.

rules.heading: Which practitioners have a page
body: A practitioner has a public page when the register lists them with at least one activity open to patients (a practice, a health centre or a hospital) at an address. People without a fixed place of practice keep a record they can claim, but no public page.
Pages show facts only, in a neutral order: there are no ratings, no reviews and no paid ranking.

correct.heading: Correcting an error
body: Most facts come from registers kept by others, so the lasting fix is made at the source. The page follows at the next weekly import.
list: Name, profession, specialty, place of practice and phone: the practitioner updates their registration with their Ordre (or the body that registered them in the RPPS).
Agreement sector, OPTAM and Carte Vitale: they come from the Assurance Maladie directory (ameli.fr).
Name and address of an establishment: they come from the FINESS register, kept by the regional health agencies.
Practitioners can also claim their page from the practitioners’ area, then complete it and correct what is shown.
correct.formBody: Tell us what is wrong on a page. Your message is encrypted and read by the Apercura team only.

remove.heading: Objecting to a page
body: Under article 21 of the GDPR, a practitioner can object to the publication of their page. Apercura publishes the directory on the basis of a legitimate interest: informing the public from public data.

An unclaimed page will be hidden as soon as the request is received, then deleted after a light check of the request. A claimed page can be removed by its holder at any time. A removed page is deleted with its data; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the RPPS number, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that the page does not come back with the next imports. A holder who removes their page also keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, title, profession and RPPS number shown in their space, their claim and the places their agenda uses.

AccessibilityPage.metaDescription: Accessibility statement of Apercura: partially conforming to RGAA 4.1, audit in progress, what was checked, how to report a problem and your recourse.
AccessibilityPage.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityPage.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where it stands: a self-assessment is done, the full audit is in progress.

commitment.heading: Commitment
body: The publisher of Apercura is committed to making the site accessible. It aims to conform to the French accessibility framework (RGAA 4.1) and to WCAG 2.2 level AA on every page.
Patient pages use body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, a visible focus, and nothing on them relies on colour alone.

status.heading: Compliance status
body: The site partially conforms to RGAA 4.1. This status rests on a self-assessment and on automated tests, not yet on a full audit: the conformance rate will be published at the end of the manual audit, which is in progress.
This statement is interim. It will be completed after the audit, with the list of non-conforming content.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type and every booking step, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus: search, booking, the practitioners’ agenda.

Journeys read by a virtual screen reader: home, results, a practitioner’s page, every booking step, the appointment page, the day and week agenda (headings, regions, fields read with their label, announcements).
Display at 390 px wide without horizontal scrolling, checked on the pages that needed it.
Lighthouse accessibility scores of the home page, a practitioner page and a listing.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver (macOS and iOS) and NVDA (Windows) screen readers.
The audit of the 106 RGAA criteria on a representative sample of pages.
The results map: it complements the results table, which holds the same information, but it is not evaluated yet.

technologies.heading: Technologies used
body: HTML, CSS, WAI-ARIA and JavaScript. Search and the directory pages also work without JavaScript. Automated tests use Chromium; VoiceOver with Safari and NVDA with Firefox will be tested during the audit.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If you cannot access some content or a service, write to us at the address below: we will offer you an alternative and fix the page.

PrivacyPage.metaDescription: Data processed by Apercura, purposes, legal bases, retention, recipients, cookies and your rights, including objection.
PrivacyPage.title: Privacy
PrivacyPage.lead: Apercura collects as little as it can. This policy says what data is processed, why, for how long, by whom, and how to exercise your rights. The French version is binding.

roles.heading: Who is responsible
body: For the public directory, practitioner accounts, error reports and removal requests, the publisher of the site is the data controller.

For online appointments, each practitioner is the controller of their patients’ data. The publisher processes it on their behalf, as a processor, under the processing agreement included in the practitioner terms (GDPR article 28).

practitioners.heading: Directory: data about practitioners
body: Data: last name, first name, title, RPPS number, profession, specialties and skills, places and modes of practice, published phone numbers, conventionnement sector, OPTAM membership and Carte Vitale acceptance. A practitioner who claims their page can add their hours, fees, languages, a photo and a presentation.
Sources: the Annuaire Santé of the Agence du numérique en santé, the FINESS register and the Assurance Maladie directory, reused under the Licence Ouverte 2.0 and refreshed every week.
Purpose: letting the public find a health practitioner, where they practise and how to reach them. Legal basis: the legitimate interest of informing the public from public data (GDPR article 6.1.f).

Retention: as long as the practitioner is listed in the public registers. An unclaimed page disappears after two weekly updates in which the practitioner is no longer in the register; a page removed after an objection is deleted at once and never published again: all that is kept is a record of the removal (the RPPS number, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when).
Information: writing to every practitioner would take a disproportionate effort (GDPR article 14.5.b). They are informed by the data page, a notice on every page and this policy.

accounts.heading: Practitioner accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, Pro Santé Connect identity, supporting documents sent to claim a page, team members, and the log of access to patient data.

Purposes: managing the account, checking that a page is claimed by the right practitioner and protecting access to patient data. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6.1.b) and the legitimate interest of securing the service (article 6.1.f).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision; the access log is erased after one year.

patients.heading: Appointments: data about patients
body: Data: first name, last name, email address, phone, whether it is a first visit, the reason chosen among the practitioner’s, date and time of the appointment. The practitioner may ask for less; no patient account is created.

Purposes: booking the appointment, sending the confirmation code, the confirmation and the reminder, and letting the patient cancel or move it. The practitioner, as controller, sets the legal basis; this data is health data (GDPR article 9).
Protection: this data is encrypted at the application level, with a key of its own for each practice, and every reading is logged. Emails contain neither the specialty nor the reason.
Retention: an unconfirmed booking is erased after 24 hours; the data of an appointment is erased 90 days after its date by default (30 to 365 days, as the practitioner sets it).

reports.heading: Error reports and removal requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and, for a removal request, the page concerned. Free text is encrypted.

Purposes: correcting reported errors and applying objections. Legal bases: the legitimate interest of publishing accurate information (article 6.1.f) and the right to object (article 21). Retention: the time needed to handle the request, then a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed and a rejected removal request one year after its decision. Once an objection is confirmed, or a holder removes their page, the page and the data about the practitioner are deleted at once, the removal requests, the reports and the claims of other people included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the RPPS number, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that the next imports skip the practitioner and the page is never published again. If the objection is withdrawn, that record is deleted and the page comes back with the next weekly update. Two things can still hold what is left of the page, never published: the account of a holder who removed it, which keeps the name, title, profession, RPPS number and page address shown in their space, their claim (its documents are deleted 30 days after its decision, like any claim's) and the places their agenda uses, until the account is deleted; and the agenda of a practice, which keeps the same identity until the practice is closed. That remainder is then deleted, at the latest with the next weekly update.

“I am this practitioner” requests: the name, the professional email address, the phone number when given, the message and the page concerned, encrypted. Purpose: helping a practitioner who cannot claim their page online. Legal basis: the legitimate interest of keeping the directory up to date with the practitioners concerned (article 6.1.f). Retention: 12 months after the last exchange.

security.heading: Security and technical data
body: Practitioner sessions record a truncated IP address (the network, not the device) and the browser used, to protect their account. To limit abuse, the site transforms IP addresses with a keyed function before counting them, and never stores them as such; each counter is deleted once its window (a minute to a day) has elapsed. The host keeps its own technical logs under its contract.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and is never used for advertising. Only these receive it, each for its own part: the publisher’s team (with no access to patient data), the practitioner and their team for their appointments, and the processors below.

Maps are loaded from a tile server (OpenFreeMap by default), which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website does, but no account or appointment data. Signing in with Pro Santé Connect goes through the Agence du numérique en santé.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: None: all data, health data included, is hosted and processed in the European Economic Area and is not transferred outside it. Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

transfersHds.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: None: data is hosted and processed in the European Economic Area, and health data in France. Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

cookies.heading: Cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in practitioners, the chosen language, and a cookie that limits a booking in progress to one browser (24 hours). No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers: no consent banner is needed.

Statistics of claimed pages: each view adds one to the page’s total for the day, with no cookie or identifier; no IP address and no browser is recorded, and browsers that ask not to be tracked (Global Privacy Control, Do Not Track) are not counted. Only the page’s holder sees these totals, kept 13 months.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing and to receive it in a portable format, object to its processing, and set directives on what happens to it after your death. Practitioners can export their account data from their space.

Write to the address below. For an appointment, preferably contact the practitioner, who is responsible for that data; if you write to us, we forward the request to them. You will get an answer within one month.
If you believe your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the CNIL.

objection.heading: Objecting to a directory page
body: A practitioner can object to the publication of their page without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: it is hidden at once, then deleted after a light check, and the updates never publish it again. If it is claimed, only its holder can remove it, from their space.

changes.heading: Updates to this policy
body: This policy is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer and by the data protection officer before appointments open; every version is dated.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura is a free directory of health practitioners registered in France, built from public open data, with free online booking for the practitioners who open it. It is published by the entity named in the legal notice.
Using the directory or booking an appointment requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from public registers, in a neutral order. They carry no ratings, reviews, advertising or paid ranking.
The information may contain errors or be out of date: check it with the practitioner before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

fees.heading: Fees and conventionnement
body: Pages state the conventionnement sector and OPTAM membership as the Assurance Maladie publishes them, and link to ameli.fr to check them. Bookable pages also show the regulatory notice required by the order of 30 May 2018 (article 5).
The exact wording of that notice will be copied verbatim after the legal review: until then, it appears below as a field to fill in.

booking.heading: Booking an appointment
body: An appointment is confirmed with a code sent by email. Depending on the practitioner’s setting, it is confirmed at once or after they accept it. The link received by email lets you cancel or move it up to the deadline the practitioner sets.

Give accurate contact details and let the practice know if you cannot come. The times offered are the ones the practitioner publishes: the publisher guarantees neither their availability nor that the appointment takes place, which is the practitioner’s responsibility.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 15 (SAMU) or 112.

practitioners.heading: For practitioners
body: Claiming a page and opening booking are free. Claiming a page requires proof of identity: Pro Santé Connect, the email address in the register, or a document checked by a person.

The practitioner is responsible for the information they add to their page. It must stay factual, fair and up to date, as the codes of professional conduct require; they state their fees and payment methods before opening their agenda.

For appointments, the practitioner is the controller of their patients’ data and the publisher their processor. The processing clauses of GDPR article 28 are annexed to the practitioner terms; they are being drafted and will be signed before appointments open.
The practitioner can export their account data and ask for the account to be closed at any time.

removal.heading: Removing a page
body: A practitioner can ask for their page to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The publisher does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it: the service may be interrupted for maintenance or after an incident. It is not responsible for the information practitioners add nor for the appointments themselves. These limits will be specified during the legal review.

PrivacyAt.title: Privacy
PrivacyAt.lead: What data the Austrian pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights (GDPR articles 13 and 14).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The media owner named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of practitioner accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about doctors and dentists
body: Data: title, first and last name, profession and specialty, the address of each practice, its location and, in Vienna, the practice phone number, as the sources publish them. A doctor who claims their page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.
Identifiers: the Vienna and Styria lists give each doctor a number; the Salzburg lists give none, so the identifier of a Salzburg page is derived from the names it lists.
Purpose: letting the public find a doctor or dentist, where they practise and how to reach them. Legal basis: legitimate interest (GDPR article 6 (1) (f)), set out below.

Retention: as long as the practitioner appears in the source. A page disappears after two weekly updates in which the practitioner is no longer in the source; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the practitioners themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would take a disproportionate effort (article 14 (5) (b)): they are informed by this policy, the data page and a notice on every page.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from open government data published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, reused with the attribution each publisher requires:

balancing.heading: Balancing of interests
body: Interest: patients and the public need to know which doctors practise where, a need the Länder already meet by publishing these lists as open data.
Necessity: only the professional data of the lists is shown, the data a practice makes public anyway; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.
Safeguards: a neutral order, no advertising, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every update of the lists.

Expectations: doctors with a practice in Austria are listed in the public lists of their chamber, published by law (Ärztegesetz 1998, § 27); a directory repeating that information is to be expected. Weighing these points, the interest of the public prevails, and any doctor can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Practitioner accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (the chamber ID card or a confirmation of the chamber) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right practitioner. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6 (1) (b)) and the legitimate interest of securing the service (article 6 (1) (f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for an “I am this practitioner” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.

Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a practitioner who cannot claim their page online. Legal bases: legitimate interest (article 6 (1) (f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about the person are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, title, profession and identifier shown in their space, their claim and the places their agenda uses, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in practitioners and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; practitioner sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the publisher’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: None: the data is hosted and processed in the European Economic Area. Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can lodge a complaint with the Austrian Data Protection Authority (Datenschutzbehörde), Barichgasse 40-42, 1030 Vienna, phone +43 1 52 152-0, dsb@dsb.gv.at, or with the authority of your place of residence or work in the European Union.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: A doctor or dentist can object to the publication of their page at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the lists never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.lead: Your practitioner space: your page, your agenda, your team.
signIn.asideFactor: Every account that can reach appointments needs a second factor: a code from an authenticator app or a passkey.
signIn.asidePasskey: A passkey is kept on your phone or computer and unlocked with your fingerprint, face or PIN.
signIn.passkeyHint: No password needed: your device confirms it is you.
signIn.totpLead: Open your authenticator app and enter the 6-digit code shown for Apercura.
signIn.backupLead: Each backup code works once. You received them when you set up your authenticator app.
signIn.pscHint: Once linked to your account from a claim, your e-CPS app or CPS card signs you in without another code.
signIn.psc: Sign in with Pro Santé Connect
signIn.pscFailed: Pro Santé Connect sign-in did not work. Link it to your account from your claim first, or sign in with your password.

signUp.title: Create an account
signUp.lead: Free for practitioners and their assistants.
signUp.asideSteps: Three steps: create the account, confirm your email address, then set up a second factor.
signUp.asideFree: Creating an account does not change any public page. Claiming your page comes next.
signUp.name: First and last name
signUp.emailHint: We send a confirmation link to this address.
signUp.passwordHint: At least {min} characters. A long sentence is easy to remember.
signUp.sentTitle: We sent a confirmation link to {email}.
signUp.sentBody: Open the email and follow the link within an hour. Then sign in to set up your second factor.
signUp.sentHint: Nothing after a few minutes? Check your spam folder, or sign in: we will send a new link.

verifyEmail.title: Email confirmation
verifyEmail.successBody: Sign in with your password to set up your second factor.
verifyEmail.errorBody: It may have expired or been used already. Sign in: we will send you a new link.

challenge.title: Confirm it is you
challenge.lead: Your account has a second factor: use it to open your space.
challenge.aside: Your password alone is not enough to reach appointments.
challenge.passkeyLead: Your device asks for your fingerprint, face or PIN.
challenge.otherHeading: Not you, or no access to your factor?
challenge.otherLead: Sign out. Recovering an account means verifying your identity again.

security.title: Security
security.lead: How you sign in, and where you are signed in.
security.enrolLead: One last step before your space: set up a second factor.
security.enrolTitle: Choose a second factor to continue
security.enrolBody: Apercura asks every account that can reach appointments for one. An authenticator app or a passkey both work; you can add the other later.

totp.heading: Authenticator app
totp.lead: An app on your phone (for example FreeOTP, Aegis or Google Authenticator) shows a new 6-digit code every 30 seconds.
totp.enabledTitle: The authenticator app is set up.
totp.enabledBody: You will be asked for a code each time you sign in with your password.
totp.scanLead: In your authenticator app, add an account and scan this code. If you cannot scan it, type the setup key.
totp.qrLabel: QR code to add Apercura to your authenticator app
totp.codesLead: If you lose your phone, each of these codes lets you sign in once. Print them or store them in a password manager; they are shown only now.
totp.confirmHeading: 3. Enter the code shown by the app
totp.passwordHint: We ask for it again before changing how you sign in.

passkeys.heading: Passkeys
passkeys.lead: A passkey stays on your phone, computer or security key and is unlocked with your fingerprint, face or PIN. Nothing to type, nothing to steal.
passkeys.name: Name

sessions.heading: Where you are signed in
sessions.lead: A session ends after 12 hours without use. Sign out any session you do not recognise.
sessions.everywhereHint: Lost a device or shared your password? Sign out of every session, this one included.

claimRegistryLink.title: Is this the practice of {practitioner}?
body: Someone has asked to manage the Apercura page of {practitioner}. This email was sent to the address the national register publishes for this practice.
If the request comes from {practitioner}, open the link and confirm it. The page is then verified.
notes: Not expected? Ignore this email: nothing changes and the page stays as it is.

claimReceived.subject: Your claim is in review
claimReceived.title: Your claim is in review
body: Hello {name},

We have received your claim and its documents. A member of the Apercura team will call the practice at the number published in the national register and ask for the code shown in your space. Keep it at hand.
We review claims within 48 hours on working days.

claimVerified.subject: Your page is verified
claimVerified.title: Your page is verified
body: Hello {name},
Your page now carries the verified stamp. Check the imported information, complete your fees and payment methods, then publish your page.

claimRejected.subject: Your claim was not accepted
claimRejected.title: Your claim was not accepted
body: Hello {name},
We could not verify your claim. Reason given by the reviewer: {reason}
You can open a new claim from your space, for instance with Pro Santé Connect.

claimSuperseded.subject: Your access to a page was withdrawn
claimSuperseded.title: Your access to a page was withdrawn
body: Hello {name},
Another account proved that it belongs to the practitioner of a page your account managed. Your account is frozen and its access to the practice was removed.
If you are the practitioner, contact us: your account can only be recovered with a new identity verification.

removalReceived.subject: Your removal request was received
removalReceived.title: Your removal request was received
body: The page is hidden from now on: it is no longer shown, indexed or listed.
We check the request and answer within one month at most. Once it is confirmed, the page is deleted; a deleted page does not come back with the next import of the register.

removalConfirmed.subject: The page was deleted
removalConfirmed.title: The page was deleted
body: The page you asked us to remove has been deleted from Apercura. It will not come back with the next import of the register.

removalRejected.subject: Your removal request was not accepted
removalRejected.title: Your removal request was not accepted
body: We could not confirm your removal request, so the page is shown again. Reason: {reason}
If you are the practitioner, you can also claim the page and remove it yourself from your space.

teamInvitation.subject: {inviter} invites you to join {practice}
teamInvitation.title: Join the team of {practice}
body: Hello,
{inviter} invites you to join {practice} on Apercura, as {role}.
To join, sign in or create your account with this email address, then set up a second factor (an authenticator app or a passkey): it protects the patients’ details you will see.
notes: You did not expect it? Ignore this email: nothing happens without you.

contactReceived.subject: Your request was received
contactReceived.title: Your request was received
body: Hello,
We have received your request about a page of the Apercura directory. A member of the team gets back to you to check your identity and help you claim the page.
If you did not send this request, ignore this email: no page and no account was changed.

psc.title: Pro Santé Connect
psc.summary: With your e-CPS app or your CPS card. Verified at once, and online booking can open straight away.

registry_email.sent: Link sent. It works for 24 hours.
registry_email.done: The practice's mailbox confirmed the claim.

document.title: A document and a phone call
document.summary: A photo of your CPS card or your registration certificate from your Ordre, then a call to the practice's number as published in the register. Reviewed within 48 hours; booking opens 7 days later.
document.lead: Send a photo of your CPS card or your registration certificate from your Ordre. It is encrypted before it is stored, and deleted 30 days after the decision.

phone_callback.title: Phone callback
phone_callback.lead: During the review, a member of our team calls the practice at {phone}, the number in the register (never a number you give us). Whoever answers reads out the code shown here.
phone_callback.hint: Show it when you are at the practice, or give it to whoever answers its phone. Asking for a new one cancels the previous one.
phone_callback.codeHint: Keep it on screen or note it down: for your security we only show it now.
phone_callback.done: The phone callback confirmed the claim.

booking.title: Opening hours and booking
booking.lead: Patients book on your page once your agenda is open. Before it can open, your page must state your fees and the payment methods you accept.

booking.settingsLink: Set up opening hours and booking

publish.shareLead: Let people know about your page: a link, a QR code and a waiting-room poster are ready.

PrivacyGb.title: Privacy notice
PrivacyGb.lead: What data the UK pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The service provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of practice accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about practices
body: Data: the name of the practice, its kind (GP practice, dental practice, pharmacy), the address of each site, including the branch surgeries of a GP practice, its location by postcode and its telephone number where the source gives one, as NHS England (Organisation Data Service), Public Health Scotland and the Business Services Organisation publish them. A practice that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Identifiers: the code each source gives the practice (an ODS code in England and Wales, a Public Health Scotland or Business Services Organisation number elsewhere); Northern Ireland’s dental list gives none, so the identifier of such a page is derived from its address.
Purpose: letting the public find a practice, where it is and how to reach it. Lawful basis: legitimate interests (UK GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.

Retention: as long as the practice appears in its source. A page disappears after two weekly updates in which the practice is no longer in its source; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the practices themselves (UK GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(e)); as article 14(7) asks, this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Practices, not people
body: The UK pages list practices, never clinicians: the Open Government Licence under which the sources are published does not cover personal data, and the registers of individual doctors, dentists and nurses are not open data.

Some practices are published under the name of the person who runs them (for example “Dr A Example & Partners”). Such a practice is shown under the name of its premises, else its street, else its town, and the person’s name is never stored. The sources’ lists of named clinicians (Public Health Scotland’s GP contact details, the Business Services Organisation’s dentist list) are not imported.
A practice run by one person can still be about that person: its page follows the safeguards below, and it can be removed on request.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from open government data published under the Open Government Licence v3.0, reused with the attribution statement of each publisher:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients and the public need to know which practices are where and how to reach them, a need the NHS bodies already meet by publishing these lists as open data.
Necessity: only the organisation data of the lists is shown, the data a practice makes public anyway; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews, no clinician.

Balance: a neutral order, no advertising, a name that never names a person, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every update of the lists. A practice listed by the NHS expects to be found in a directory repeating that information. Weighing these points, the interests of the public prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Practice accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the practice or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right practice. Lawful bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for an “I run this practice” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a practice that cannot claim its page online. Lawful bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, profession and identifier shown in their space, their claim and the places their agenda uses, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in practices and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; practice sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the United Kingdom
body: The data is hosted and processed in the European Economic Area. A transfer from the United Kingdom to an EEA state is approved by UK law (Data Protection Act 2018, schedule 21, paragraphs 4 and 5, under UK GDPR article 45A): no other safeguard is needed. Nothing is transferred elsewhere; any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can make a complaint to us at the same address (Data Protection Act 2018, section 164A), and to the Information Commissioner’s Office, the UK’s supervisory authority: Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire SK9 5AF, helpline 0303 123 1113, ico.org.uk.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (UK GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the lists never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

service.heading: The service

content.heading: What the pages contain

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of facility accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about facilities
body: Data: the name of the hospital, clinic or pharmacy as the directory publishes it, its kind, its departments, whether it takes part in emergency care and at which level, the kind of its operator (public, non-profit or private) and of the facility, its address and its telephone number when it is that facility’s own; for a pharmacy of Thuringia, whether it is a main pharmacy or a branch and how accessible it is. A facility that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Never stored, although the sources publish them: the e-mail and web addresses, the name of the operator, the number of beds and the pseudonymous identifier the hospital directory draws anew every year. A telephone number that a source gives for more than three facilities is a head office’s and is not shown. The hospital directory publishes no coordinates: a hospital or clinic is placed at the geographic centre of its municipality, never at its address; a pharmacy is placed at the point its Land publishes.

Identifier: a key that names the source and the facility (for example k0a1b2c3d4e), at the end of the page’s address. The sources publish no national number: for a hospital or clinic the key is derived from its municipality, address and names; for a pharmacy of Thuringia it is the number of its file at the supervising authority.
Purpose: letting the public find a hospital, a clinic or a pharmacy, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.
Retention: as long as the facility appears in its source. A page disappears when an edition of its source no longer lists the facility; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the facilities themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(b)); this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Facilities, and the people they name
body: A German page is a facility, never a person’s profile: Germany’s registers of doctors and dentists are not open, and no person is listed. A pharmacy belongs to a pharmacist; when its name as the Land publishes it includes the owner’s name, the page shows it, as a professional detail.

Nothing else about any person is collected: no date of birth, no identity or tax number, no private address, no ratings and no reviews. No patient’s data, and no health data, is processed by the directory.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Hospitals and clinics come from the directory of hospitals and of prevention and rehabilitation clinics (Verzeichnis der Krankenhäuser und Vorsorge- oder Rehabilitationseinrichtungen) that the Federal Statistical Office publishes every year on behalf of the statistical offices of the Federation and the Länder; its terms allow reproduction and distribution, even in part, with the source. Pharmacies come from the lists of the supervising authorities of Thuringia (CC BY 4.0) and Brandenburg (Data licence Germany – Attribution – Version 2.0); the other Länder publish no current list as open data, so their pharmacies are not listed. Places come from Destatis’s directory of municipalities. Each source is reused with its attribution:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients need to know which hospitals, clinics and pharmacies are where, what care they offer and how to reach them, a need the State already meets by publishing these directories.
Necessity: only the facility’s data from the directories is shown, the data they publish anyway, and less of it; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.

Balance: a neutral order, no advertising, the minimum of the directories’ fields, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every edition of the directories. A facility listed in a public directory expects to be found in a directory repeating that information. Weighing these points, the interests of patients prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Facility accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right facility. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a facility that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set (§ 25(2) TDDDG): the session of signed-in facilities and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; facility sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, under a contract that meets GDPR article 28. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: Data is transferred outside the European Union and the European Economic Area only under the safeguards of chapter V of the GDPR (an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses). Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can also lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (GDPR article 77), in particular the one of the Land where you live. The data protection conference (Datenschutzkonferenz) lists the authorities of the Federation and the Länder.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the directories never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

PrivacyEs.title: Privacy
PrivacyEs.lead: What data the Spanish pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Ley Orgánica 3/2018 on personal data protection and digital rights (LOPDGDD).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The operator named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of centre accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about health centres
body: Data: the name of the centre as it is registered, its kind (health centre, dental clinic, pharmacy…), its care units (“oferta asistencial”), whether it is public or private, its address and municipality, and its telephone number when it is that centre’s own, as the General Register of health centres, services and establishments (REGCESS) of the Ministry of Health publishes them. A centre that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Never stored, although the register publishes them: the centre’s e-mail address and fax, its regional code and the dates of its authorisations. A telephone number that the register gives for more than three centres is a head office’s and is not shown. The register publishes no coordinates: a centre is placed at its municipality’s main population centre, never at its address.
Identifier: the normalised centre code the register gives each centre (CCN), at the end of the page’s address.
Purpose: letting the public find a health centre, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.

Retention: as long as the centre appears in the register. A page disappears after two updates in which the centre is no longer in the register; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the centres themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(b)); this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Centres, and the people they name
body: A Spanish page is a health centre, the unit of the register, never a person’s profile. Many practices and pharmacies belong to a professional working on their own account, and are registered under that person’s name (for example “Ana María Ejemplo Sanz”): such a page names the person, and is about them.

Only the centre’s registered name is shown, as the register publishes it, with its professional details: the data of sole traders and liberal professionals that refer to their professional activity, which article 19(3) of the LOPDGDD presumes may be processed. Nothing else about the person is collected: no date of birth, no identity or tax number, no home address other than the one the register gives as the centre’s, no ratings and no reviews.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from REGCESS, the register the Ministry of Health keeps under Real Decreto 1277/2003 on the authorisation of health centres and publishes every month; its legal notice allows reuse, commercial or not, citing the source and the date of the last update and without distorting the data (Ley 37/2007). Places come from the IGN (CC BY 4.0). Each source is reused with its attribution:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients need to know which health centres are where, what care they offer and how to reach them, a need the State already meets by keeping the register and publishing it.
Necessity: only the register’s data about the centre is shown, the data it publishes anyway; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.

Balance: a neutral order, no advertising, the minimum of the register’s fields, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every update of the register. A centre listed in a public register expects to be found in a directory repeating that information. Weighing these points, the interests of patients prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Centre accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the centre or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right centre. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a centre that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, kind and identifier shown in their space and their claim, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in centres and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; centre sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the operator’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, under a contract that meets GDPR article 28. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: Data is transferred outside the European Union and the European Economic Area only under the safeguards of chapter V of the GDPR (an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses). Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.
You can also lodge a complaint with the Spanish supervisory authority, the Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD): C/ Jorge Juan, 6, 28001 Madrid, www.aepd.es.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the register never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

changes.heading: Updates to this notice
body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer qualified in Spain and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

PrivacyCh.title: Privacy
PrivacyCh.lead: What data the Swiss pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP), in force since 1 September 2023, and its ordinance (DSV).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The provider named in the Impressum is the controller of the directory, of facility accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site. Write to the address below with any question about your data.

law.heading: Which law applies
body: The processing of the Swiss pages is subject to the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP, SR 235.1) and to the Data Protection Ordinance (DSV, SR 235.11). As the provider is established in the European Union, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies to its processing as well: a section below says what it adds.

directory.heading: Directory: data about facilities
body: Data: the facility’s name as its list publishes it; its kind (hospital or clinic site, nursing home, pharmacy); for a hospital or clinic, its type in the Federal Statistical Office’s typology, its activity types, its emergency department and intensive care unit, its outpatient and inpatient offer, the legal form group of its hospital and its operator; the category its canton’s list gives it; its address, postcode, locality, commune and canton; its phone number where its list gives one, and its position where its list gives coordinates. A facility that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.
This is data about organisations. The nFADP protects data about natural persons only: a facility’s data is personal data where its name designates a person, as the next section explains.
Purpose: letting the public find a hospital, a clinic, a nursing home or a pharmacy, where it is and what it is.
Retention: as long as the facility appears in its list. A page disappears after two imports in which the facility is no longer in it; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

people.heading: Facilities, and the people they name
body: A Swiss page is a facility, never a person’s profile. No health professional is listed: no register of individual doctors, pharmacists or other professionals is imported.

A facility’s name can designate a person, for example a pharmacy named after its pharmacist (“Apotheke Dr. Muster”): that name is then personal data, taken from a list the Confederation or a canton publishes. A page prints the name as its list publishes it, without a care-of address and what follows it, which can name someone else. Nothing else about a person is collected: the names of responsible pharmacists, the e-mail addresses and the user names of the lists’ editors are never read, and there is no date of birth, no home address, no rating and no review.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from open government data: the Federal Office of Public Health’s (FOPH) “Kennzahlen der Schweizer Spitäler 2023”, the lists of hospitals, nursing homes and pharmacies that the cantons of Zürich, Bern, Geneva, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft and Jura publish on opendata.swiss, the Federal Statistical Office’s official commune register and swisstopo’s official directory of localities with their postcodes. Each source is reused with the attribution it asks for:

grounds.heading: Principles and grounds
body: Under the nFADP, a private person may process personal data without consent as long as the processing follows the principles of articles 6 and 8 (lawfulness, good faith, proportionality, a recognisable and limited purpose, accuracy, data security) and the person concerned has not expressly objected to it (article 30(2)). Consent is not the general ground of processing, and the directory asks for none.

Where a page names a person, the provider relies on an overriding interest (article 31(1)): the public needs to know which hospitals, clinics, nursing homes and pharmacies are where, a need the Confederation and the cantons already meet by publishing these lists as open data. Only the facility’s own data is shown, in a neutral order, without advertising, ratings or reviews; an objection hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back.
Facility accounts and claims rest on the terms of use, a contract with the account holder (article 31(2)(a)), and on the provider’s interest in securing the service.

information.heading: How you are informed
body: The facility data does not come from the facilities themselves. For data not collected from the person concerned, article 19 of the nFADP asks the controller to give also the categories of data processed (paragraph 3), at the latest one month after obtaining them (paragraph 5).

This notice gives that information: the controller and its contact details, the purposes, the categories of data, the sources, the recipients, the disclosure abroad and your rights. It is linked from every page, and the data page lists each source. The people a facility’s name may designate are not known to the provider one by one: informing each of them individually would require a disproportionate effort (article 20(2)(b)).

objection.heading: Objecting to a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (nFADP articles 30(2)(b) and 32(2); GDPR article 21). If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough, on the data page or on the page itself: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the lists never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

accounts.heading: Facility accounts and claims
body: Data: e-mail address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right facility. Grounds: the terms of use (nFADP article 31(2)(a); GDPR article 6(1)(b)) and the interest in securing the service (GDPR article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact e-mail address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.

Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a facility that cannot claim its page online. Grounds: the interest in an accurate directory and the right to object (nFADP articles 31(1) and 32(2); GDPR articles 6(1)(f) and 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, kind and identifier shown in their space and their claim, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data, cookies and local storage
body: Only what the service technically needs is stored in your browser: the session cookie of signed-in facilities and, in the browser’s local storage, the light or dark display you chose, which is never sent to the server. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

Article 45c of the Telecommunications Act (TCA) asks that you be told what is stored on your device and why, and that you can refuse it: you can block or delete these items in your browser’s settings, signing in then no longer works.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; facility sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, bound by contract to process it only as the provider instructs and to keep it secure (nFADP article 9; GDPR article 28). Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

abroad.heading: Disclosure abroad
body: Data may be processed in states of the European Economic Area, whose legislation the Federal Council recognises as providing adequate protection (nFADP article 16(1) and annex 1 of the DSV): no other safeguard is needed. Nothing is disclosed elsewhere; any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated individual decisions
body: No decision about you is based exclusively on automated processing (nFADP article 21). A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask whether data about you is processed and receive it (right of access, nFADP article 25), receive the data you provided in a common electronic format or have it transmitted to another controller (article 28), have inaccurate data corrected, and have data erased or its processing or disclosure stopped (article 32). Write to the address below; access is given free of charge, within 30 days.

You can also report a processing you consider contrary to data protection rules to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC), Feldeggweg 1, 3003 Bern, www.edoeb.admin.ch, who can open an investigation (article 49).

gdpr.heading: Visitors in the European Union and the EEA
body: The GDPR applies to the provider’s processing as well, in particular for visitors in the European Union and the European Economic Area. This notice gives the information its articles 13 and 14 require; the facility data is processed on the ground of legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)), weighed as above. You can object at any time to the processing of data about you (article 21), ask for its processing to be restricted (article 18), and lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority of the state where you live or work (article 77). Requests go to the same address and are answered within one month.

body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer admitted in Switzerland and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

AccessibilityCh.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Swiss pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: The Disability Discrimination Act (BehiG, SR 151.3) requires the Confederation to make its own online services accessible; it sets no such duty for private websites, and this statement is voluntary. Its provider nevertheless aims at the standard the Confederation applies to its own sites, eCH-0059, which builds on the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, and at WCAG 2.2 level AA on every page.

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Swiss pages share the code of the French pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress.

tests.heading: What was checked

Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked

A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

sources.termsText: The terms of use of opendata.swiss

coverage.heading: Facilities covered
body: A page is a facility, never a person. What is listed depends on what each canton publishes as open data:
coverage.elsewhere: Elsewhere, no nursing home or pharmacy is listed yet, and no medical or dental practice is listed anywhere.

kinds.CH_HOSPITAL: General hospitals: university hospitals, centre care and basic care (FSO types K111 to K123)
kinds.CH_SPECIALTY_CLINIC: Specialised clinics: surgery, gynaecology and neonatology, paediatrics, geriatrics and others (K231 to K235)
kinds.CH_NURSING_HOME: Nursing homes, where a canton lists them
kinds.CH_PHARMACY: Pharmacies, where a canton lists them

excluded.heading: What is not imported, and why
body: Some data would complete the directory but cannot be reused, or is not needed:
list: Health professionals: the federal registers of the medical professions (MedReg), the psychology professions (PsyReg) and the health professions (GesReg) can be consulted one entry at a time; their bulk data needs an agreement with the FOPH, which the directory does not have. No person is listed.
Refdata’s partner data (GLN numbers of professionals and businesses): not open data; republishing it needs Refdata’s written consent.
OpenStreetMap: used for the base map only, never as a source of facilities or of their positions, since its Open Database Licence (ODbL) is share-alike.
The FOPH’s hospital figures for 2024: their terms ask for permission before any commercial use, so the 2023 edition, open with the source, is read.
Data about individuals, never: no register of people, no ratings, no reviews.

unread.heading: Fields never read
body: The lists hold some fields a page does not need, some of which name or reach a person. They are never read or stored:
list: The name of the responsible pharmacist in the canton of Basel-Landschaft’s list of pharmacies.
E-mail addresses, in every list.
The user name of the editor of each record in the canton of Jura’s file.
The figures of the FOPH’s workbook (costs, staff, cases): a page needs none of them.
A care-of or attention mention in a facility’s name, and what follows it.

locations.heading: Locations
body: Every facility is placed in its canton, district and commune, from the Federal Statistical Office’s official commune register: by the commune number where its list gives one, else by its postcode and locality, from swisstopo’s official directory of localities.

Its point is the one its list gives, converted from the Swiss national grid where needed. The FOPH’s figures and some lists give no coordinates: such a facility is shown at the point of its locality in swisstopo’s directory. No pin marks it on a map, and its distance is approximate.

identifiers.heading: Identifiers
body: Switzerland publishes no open national number of a health facility: the address of every page ends with the key of its list, after letters naming that list, so that a page can be found and checked against its source:
list: /ch/einrichtung/spital-beispiel-h123456789: a site of the FOPH’s figures, which give it no number; its key is derived from its canton, hospital, name and postcode, after h.
/ch/einrichtung/apotheke-beispiel-blp7601000000000: the Global Location Number (GLN) of a pharmacy in the canton of Basel-Landschaft’s list, after blp.

/ch/einrichtung/pflegeheim-beispiel-gee123456: the cantonal address identifier (IDPADR) of a nursing home in Geneva’s list, after gee; the identifier of a home in the canton of Zürich’s list follows zhe.
The other lists number no facility: their key is derived from the facility’s name and address, after letters naming the canton and the list (beh, bee, geh, gep, ble, bsh, bse, ju).

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the public lists: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import after the corrected list is published.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: A facility from a canton’s list: ask the cantonal office that publishes the list, named in the sources above, to correct it.
A hospital or clinic site from the FOPH’s figures: the 2023 figures are not published again; report the error with the form below.
Phone, website and opening hours: where the list gives none, a facility adds them by claiming its page.
correct.formBody: Give the address of the page and what is wrong.

remove.heading: Remove a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (nFADP articles 30(2)(b) and 32(2); GDPR article 21). An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the updates of the lists. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space. Every page also has its own removal form.

remove.formBody: Give the address of the page and an e-mail address where we can answer you.

LegalNoticeLt.title: Legal information
LegalNoticeLt.lead: Who operates the Lithuanian pages of Apercura (apercura.org/lt), as article 6 of the Law on Information Society Services (Informacinės visuomenės paslaugų įstatymas, No. X-614) asks of a provider of information society services.

provider.heading: Operator
body: The Lithuanian pages of Apercura are operated by the entity below. It runs the directory and answers for its content.

service.heading: The service
body: A free directory of licensed health-care institutions in Lithuania (hospitals, primary care centres, medical centres and clinics, dental clinics, mental health centres, rehabilitation and nursing services, laboratories and optometrists' practices), built from the licence data that the State Accreditation Service for Health Care Activities (VASPVT) publishes as open data, without advertising, with a space where an institution can complete its own page. No individual health worker and no pharmacy is listed, and no appointment is booked through Apercura in Lithuania.

editor.heading: Person responsible for the content
body: The person below is responsible for what the operator publishes. Information an institution adds to its own page is its own responsibility; as a service that stores information provided by its users, the operator answers for it only under the conditions of the Law on Information Society Services.

liability.heading: Content of the pages
body: The directory is built from the dataset “Sveikatos priežiūros įstaigų licencijų duomenys”, which VASPVT publishes on data.gov.lt under CC BY 4.0, and from the Address Register of the Republic of Lithuania (VĮ Registrų centras, CC BY 4.0). It can be incomplete or out of date: check the information with the institution before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code of Apercura is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The directory data is reused under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0): the data page lists every source with the attribution it requires.
